ceiling_directive: Prove a within-non-Gaussian lower bound matching the strong-separation length scale min{d_n^-, B_n/delta_n}, using two target-separated priors supported in N_n(delta_n) with common supplied fits.
improvement_directive: Construct and certify a within-N_n(delta_n) lower-bound experiment that yields L_N(C_n) greater than or comparable to min{d_n^-, B_n/delta_n}; this would establish necessity of the claimed shortening threshold without relying on the refuted cross-branch construction. Also replace CT1–CT2 with an explicit Gaussian subexperiment derived from primitive class conditions.
critique: The note proves a substantive union-honest adaptive interval and a non-Gaussian upper length bound, but it does not characterize the requested Pareto lower boundary: no non-Gaussian branchwise converse is delivered, so necessity of the shortening threshold remains open. The Gaussian nuisance-product lower bound is conditional on CT2, a proof-tailored assumption that directly postulates compatibility and inclusion of the cited fuzzy supports, while CT1 similarly postulates the compatible parametric path; only the two-point calculation after those assumptions is internal. Calling thm:adaptive-upper-frontier and its justification a “frontier” is therefore a stale over-claim, since the theorem supplies one attainable rate vector rather than a boundary, although the TL;DR and scope sections later disclaim a matching frontier. These missing converses and the assumed lower-experiment transfer prevent a field-tier or leading-journal contribution despite the useful upper construction and negative diagnosis of the cross-branch route. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
